SMTO-HTTP-0040 — The service rejected SMTO's sign-in request

GUID: 34f1d3fb-6768-4a62-ad55-6c2dd3494bdd
Slug: http-auth-request-rejected
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The service refused the sign-in because something in the request was wrong or missing, or because there were too many attempts. Its reply doesn't say exactly which.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store, select the HTTP connection, and check the sign-in settings: Login path, Login body format, Username field and Password field, or for OAuth Client ID, Scopes and Audience. The service rejected what the sign-in contained, so a field name, format or value is likely wrong.
  2. Compare those settings with the service's sign-in documentation, including which Login body format it expects, and correct any that differ. Each service expects its own field names and format for signing in.
  3. Save, then select Test connection. If the service said there were too many attempts, wait a few minutes before testing. Repeated failed sign-ins can make the service refuse for a while even after the fix.

What success looks like

  • Test connection shows Authenticated, and the task's request is accepted.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who set up this connection. Don't keep sending the same sign-in unchanged; it will be refused again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The authentication endpoint returned a 4xx status other than 401, 403, 404 or 405 (for example 400, 409, 422 or 429).

What this means

  • The authentication endpoint returned a 4xx status other than 401, 403, 404 or 405. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The authentication endpoint returned a 4xx status other than 401, 403, 404 or 405.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect sanitized status and structured error details, including rate limits or request validation, without inventing a credential cause.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the status code and authentication response recorded for the auth endpoint, then correct the login recipe (path, body format, username/password field names, extra login fields, or OAuth grant, scope and audience) per the target's API documentation; for 429, honor the provider's rate limit before re-testing.
  • Inspect the safe status and request fields and correct the authentication recipe using API documentation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The documented login request satisfies the specific observed rejection condition.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
